editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Tuesday, Oct 27, 2026
editions.summary: The pick of the day is Genie 4, the new world model Google DeepMind announced this morning. You steer a live, explorable scene with the keyboard and plain-language prompts (change the weather, move the camera, add a person), and for the first time the model makes the sound too: ambient noise, music and characters who talk back. It matters for designers because DeepMind's own trusted testers are using it the way creative teams work: filmmakers running live "takes" for previs, and game developers going from an idea to an explorable prototype before writing engine code. The launch post has 13,730 likes, 5,597 bookmarks and about 1.43M views in under eight hours, Sundar Pichai's post has 11,920 likes, and the Hacker News thread has 650 points. It is a research preview for now, and the realism claims are DeepMind's own. The rest of the day was about control. Microsoft's MAI-Image-2.7-Preview jumped to #3 on Arena's image-edit board, a new design-skills repo for coding agents led GitHub's daily list, and creators kept turning one AI mesh or one prompt into whole game pipelines.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: Ten Claude sessions run one indie game, a film made from 90 paintings, and a pistol rigged from a single Tripo mesh
editions.summary: The standout story today is a solo developer who runs up to ten Claude Opus 5.5 sessions on one game at the same time, each with its own branch and job, while a lead session merges the work and calls them in to play. They report 463 commits in five weeks. Around it, people kept showing work where the agent does the craft steps: Claude Code turned one Tripo mesh into a rigged, game-ready pistol, a short film was painted 90 times instead of generated as video, and the most-liked post of the day was a Seedance 2.5 character short with 488 likes.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: AI moves into the tools you already use.
editions.summary: Krea put video generation inside Adobe Premiere, Figma opened its Weave models to AI agents, and Runway's App Studio builds a creative app from a description. ComfyUI answered with an open-source character-swap app, while the MOSS-Image crowd shipped film looks and layout tools. 76 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Monday, Oct 26, 2026
editions.summary: Today's one real explosion is GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI's cheaper model for working inside apps. Its launch post reached 21,938 likes and about 2.93M views in under nine hours, the launch video passed 270,900 views in eight hours, and creators were already driving Blender with it the same afternoon. That fits the week's pattern: the biggest gains are going to tools that sit inside the apps and chats designers already use, like CapCut's coming ChatGPT plugin (7,797 likes) and Krea's chat connector, while Grok Imagine's Odyssey Episode 1 is still the week's most-liked creative post at 22,222 likes and about 7.27M views. Over the month, staying power belongs to work that teaches agents to design and animate: Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion still lead at 60,543 likes, and VoiceStudio, HyperFrames and impeccable gained a combined 90,392 GitHub stars this month. Two more design skills, Hallmark and the new MotionSites skill, were the day's fastest risers in that lane.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Monday, Oct 26, 2026
editions.summary: The pick of the day is GPT-6.1 Terra, which OpenAI released this morning. It is a cheaper, faster model built to read what is on screen and work inside apps, and OpenAI's own examples are design jobs: turning architectural and technical drawings into 3D models, editing videos and reviewing an animated film shot by shot. The launch post has 19,260 likes, 3,000 bookmarks and about 2.15M views in under six hours, and the Hacker News thread has 462 points. It matters for designers because creators were already using it in Blender within three hours: Matt Workman's roadster pipeline (image, Blender model, camera move, then a photoreal pass) drew 164 likes and 122 bookmarks. The benchmarks and prices are OpenAI's own claims. The rest of the day backs up the agent theme. Hallmark, a design skill that keeps coding agents from producing generic AI pages, topped GitHub's daily trending list with 2,235 new stars, and Kling 4.0 reached more apps as creators kept testing it against Seedance 2.5.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: An Unreal sword game directed by Opus, a wolf fixed against a 5-second clip, and an '80s ad made on one GPU
editions.summary: The standout build today is a game recipe: a developer connected Claude Opus 5.5 to Unreal Engine through MCP and had it build an open-world sword-combat prototype, with a Tripo character, Niagara trails and grass that burns where the blade lands, in what the poster says was a few days. It drew 417 likes and 471 bookmarks. The same idea of letting the agent check its own work runs through the day, from a game-jam wolf whose walk was fixed against a short Seedance reference clip to a local '80s-style commercial made in ComfyUI on a single RTX 5090.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: Video editing moves into the chat box.
editions.summary: CapCut's ChatGPT plugin announcement passed 1.4 million views, and the most-saved Kling 4 how-tos were about editing shots you already have. Locally, new MiniMax H3 nodes tackle the drift that builds up over long chained clips. 57 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Sunday, Oct 25, 2026
editions.summary: The biggest mover again is Odyssey Episode 1 from the Grok Imagine account, which nearly doubled in a day to 19,210 likes, 12,036 bookmarks and about 5.83M views. On a quiet Sunday the other real spike was explainer video: Ben AI's rundown of the latest Claude updates passed 261,000 views in 16 hours. The week still belongs to finished, editable design work and to the open stack: Canva Craft is at 1.90M views, Ideogram's vector model at 559K, and DeepSeek's updated open model holds the week's biggest launch post at 37,146 likes. Over the month, the strongest staying power is in tools that teach coding agents to design and animate: VoiceStudio gained 50,977 GitHub stars this month, HyperFrames 19,211 and impeccable 16,493, while Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion remain the month's top post at 60,552 likes. What it means: the skills and harnesses around the models are now spreading faster than most single model launches.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Sunday, Oct 25, 2026
editions.summary: The pick of the day is the gpu-unlock family. The original module for RTX 30-series cards has gone from about 3,150 GitHub stars on Saturday evening to 6,569 tonight, its Hacker News thread has grown from 195 to 336 points, and a port for RTX 4090 and 4070 Ti SUPER cards has climbed from 696 to 2,564 stars in a day. It matters because it makes the local image and video models designers actually run (MOSS-Image, Qwen-Image, MiniMax H3) faster on cards people already own, at no cost. It is also risky: it is Linux only, the projects call themselves experimental, and the newer ports warn that full-speed tensor cores can damage hardware. The rest of the day was quiet. Lab accounts stayed silent, the most-liked creative posts on X were Seedance 2.5 clips with a few hundred likes each, and the most-watched design-adjacent video was a roundup of Claude updates with 205,848 views in 13 hours.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: A phone-sized 3D platformer in eight steps, a toddler-founder ad format, and a laser game an agent could debug
editions.summary: The most copyable builds today are recipes. One developer shows eight steps to an Ori-style platformer that runs on a phone, from GPT Image mood boards through Tripo and Blender to Opus 5.5 code. Another swaps a real founder ad for his 2-year-old self with Nano Banana Pro and Wan 3.0, and ScreenPlink, a laser shooting game built with Claude Code, solved debugging a physical-world app by giving the agent an MCP server that returns raw measurements. On a quiet Sunday most of the evidence comes from creators describing their own work, so costs and results are labelled as claims.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: Free speed for the GPU you already own, now for older cards too.
editions.summary: The RTX 30-series BF16 unlock passed 4,700 stars and was ported to the older Turing cards, with louder warnings about hardware risk. MiniMax H3 video now runs natively on Apple silicon through ComfyUI nodes, and MOSS-Image got native 4MP tests and a LoRA recipe. 52 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Saturday, Oct 24, 2026
editions.summary: The biggest mover of the last 24 hours is Odyssey Episode 1, a series episode from the Grok Imagine account whose post has climbed to 10,308 likes, 4,969 bookmarks and about 1.86M views. This week the pattern was design tools building for finished, editable work: Canva's first image model, Craft, hit 3,228 likes and 1.87M views, Ideogram's vector model reached 546K views, and Figma shipped Code Layers that turn a design layer into interactive code. At the same time the open stack kept gaining ground: DeepSeek's updated open model remains the week's biggest launch post at 37,122 likes, Kimi K3.1 Pro passed 1,000 points on Hacker News, and a free unlock for older RTX 30-series cards is at 3,153 stars after six days. The month is still shaped by prompt-to-motion and prompt-to-3D, led by Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion and by Google's Gemini 4 Argon demos, which have passed 10.9M and 8.7M views. What it means: the quick demo is no longer the hard part, so the edge is moving to who can hand over something a client can edit.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Saturday, Oct 24, 2026
editions.summary: The pick of the day is Hy-Nomas, Tencent's open-source video world model, which you steer with text prompts and camera paths instead of rendering a clip and hoping. The launch post has 846 likes, 497 bookmarks and about 48.9K views, and a community port already runs it inside ComfyUI with WASD keys. Tencent says it keeps a memory of the world over long runs and is built to run on consumer GPUs; the repo lists a single RTX 4090 with quantised weights. It beats the day's other big stories because it is free, Apache 2.0, and people could build on it within hours. The rest of the list shows what the community is doing with the wider stack: a thread of ten design and motion repos was bookmarked 2,844 times, a no-code builder shared a full eight-step game pipeline, and a free module is making older RTX 30-series cards faster. Treat the world model's quality as unproven: the technical report isn't out yet, and so far the demos come from Tencent and early adopters.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: A $143 music video with its receipts, one shader layer per prompt, and the cheap model that missed the brief
editions.summary: DOWNFORCE is a 3-minute hype edit for a Suno song, cut from footage of the Oct 15 Tesla Roadster demo plus generated shots, with Claude Code acting as production lead. Its makers published the whole production record: about 13 hours, 172 agent launches and $143.17 of a $200 budget, plus a list of what didn't work. The same habit runs through today's other real-world uses. Creators post the time and the bill for every run, and they build big things one small step at a time.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: A world you can steer, and free speed for the GPU you already own.
editions.summary: Tencent open-sourced Hy-Nomas, an interactive video world model you guide with text and camera moves, and the community had it running in ComfyUI on 12 GB cards within hours. A free Linux kernel module made BF16 image and video work 46 to 59 percent faster on RTX 30-series cards in public tests. 93 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Friday, Oct 23, 2026
editions.summary: The month still belongs to design you ask for in plain words. Claude Motion and Claude Dashboards, which turn a prompt into an animated explainer or a live dashboard, remain the most-liked and most-saved AI design launch of the past month by a wide margin, and Google's video of Gemini 4 Argon building a 3D world in Blender has now passed 7.7 million views. This week the story shifted to who owns the model. Canva shipped Craft, its first image model built for design work, a day after Ideogram released its first vector model, so two design companies now train models aimed at editable, client-ready output rather than pretty pictures. At the same time the open side surged: DeepSeek's updated open model became the week's biggest launch post, creators are calling it a new benchmark for motion design, and on GitHub an agent toolkit for taking apart apps and games gained more than 88,000 stars in seven days. What it means: the gap between a rough idea and a finished, editable piece keeps shrinking, so the edge is moving to taste, a clear brief and knowing which model to point at which job.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Friday, Oct 23, 2026
editions.summary: The design story of the day is Canva Craft, the first image model Canva has built itself. Canva says Craft plans the composition first and only then renders the picture, which is why it handles layouts and lettering better than models that go straight from prompt to pixels. It debuted at #4 on Design Arena's image leaderboard with an Elo score of 1,340, first of 87 models for portraits and first of 85 for landscapes, and the launch post passed 1.8 million views. It lands one day after Ideogram's first vector model, so in 48 hours two design companies shipped models aimed at finished, editable design work rather than pretty pictures. That matters because the gap between "AI made an image" and "I can hand this to a client" is mostly about text, layout and editability, and that's exactly what both launches go after. Treat the rankings as early: they come from the companies and one leaderboard, and nobody has run an independent test yet.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: Grey mannequins for AI actors, a one-person voxel studio, and the work of keeping one look
editions.summary: The most reusable tip in this window came from a post almost nobody saw. A team kept AI video actors on their marks by showing a grey-mannequin blocking pass for only the first few steps of generation. Around it, creators laid out full pipelines: a voxel short built through Blender and Remotion, and a motion-graphics setup that stops Claude Code drifting. Spec ads went out for brands that never asked, and Kling 4.0 against Seedance 2.5 tests disagreed with each other. Gaussian splats kept moving from demos into real jobs, from a collapsed-wall survey to an event pitch.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: The day design tools started taking orders from AI agents.
editions.summary: Anthropic gave the Agent Skills standard to the Linux Foundation, MiniMax opened its Design canvas to agents through MCP, and Google had Gemini 4 Argon build a cathedral in Blender through MCP. 55 verified items from about 7 AM PT on Oct 22 to 7 AM PT on Oct 23.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Tuesday, Oct 20, 2026
editions.summary: Gemini 4 Argon was the loudest AI launch of the week. Sundar Pichai's launch post on Oct 13 has more than 28,000 likes, and Google's own demo videos, a webcam you play like a synthesizer and a 3D pagoda built in Blender from one prompt, have racked up about 17.6 million and 8.3 million YouTube views. On Oct 20 itself, Argon came back with a 3D periodic table that animates in time with Tom Lehrer's "The Elements". But when people decide what to keep, they keep Claude. Over the past month, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Motion are still the most-liked and most-saved design launches by far. This week's most-bookmarked creative post was a single Opus 5.5 prompt billed as a "$400/hr motion graphics designer", and creators shipped a 475-demo gallery and a 25-minute anime written entirely in code. The backlash grew alongside the hype. Kotaku's report on vibe-coded game decompiles and ports spread widely, and a widely shared reminder told newcomers that an AI game needs to be fun before it needs fancy art. What it means: views follow the big labs' demos, but saves follow prompts and repos you can reuse tomorrow.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Tuesday, Oct 20, 2026
editions.summary: The design story of Oct 20 is Vyb, the first model from Coco Labs. Co-founder Anusha Ramesh says she launched Google's first image and video generation models before spending two years building it in stealth. Vyb doesn't paint a flat picture. It builds a design in layers from your own logo, fonts, colors and product photos, so text stays text, graphics stay vectors and photos are never redrawn, and the result exports to Figma. The launch post reached about 3.66 million views, the biggest view count in this edition. It landed the same morning Krea said its in-house Krea 3 model had reached the top tier of the image-editing arenas, and Bria shipped Fibo 2.0 as an open-weights editing model. Taken together, Oct 20 was the day the pitch moved from prettier pictures to designs that keep your brand and stay editable. Treat the numbers carefully: Vyb's head-to-head scores are its own, access is through a waitlist, and nobody independent has tested it yet. The most-liked pick in this edition is something else: Google DeepMind's 3D periodic table built by Gemini 4 Argon and synced to Tom Lehrer's song "The Elements".

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: An editor's client folder becomes the brief, a $297 lead, and the stills you check before you render
editions.summary: The clearest real-world account in this window comes from documentary editor Chris Cardoza. Claude Code builds his on-brand titles, charts and end cards from a folder of client material, while he still makes the cut in Final Cut Pro. Elsewhere, an agency reports that a lead-gen client's cost per lead fell from $500 to $297 in 30 days after switching to AI animation ads. Motion designers show how to make agents check their own frames, and MOSS-Image dominated the image posts.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: AI Design Daily: Tue Oct 20, 2026 (morning sweep)
editions.summary: Window: about 24 hours, from the morning of Oct 19 to the morning of Oct 20 (PT). Items marked ⏪ are a little older (Oct 13–18) and are here because they're trending in this window or got a real update. Every link was opened or returned by a tool. Engagement numbers were read on the morning of Oct 20 (PT) and will keep changing. Sources: X, YouTube, GitHub (trending, new repos and API), Hugging Face, Reddit (subreddit feeds), Product Hunt, Hacker News, and the web.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Monday, Oct 19, 2026
editions.summary: The biggest AI design post of the past month came from a lab. On Oct 8, Claude Dashboards and Claude Motion went into beta, letting anyone ask Claude for an animated explainer or a live dashboard, and the announcement drew more than 60,000 likes and almost 40,000 bookmarks. For a month the hottest design work has been animation, 3D and UI written as code, and this week the big labs leaned in hard. Google's own video of Gemini 4 Argon building a 3D world in Blender passed 4.19 million views in six days. DeepSeek's open model is now the cheap option creators race against both. The new part this week is sound and editing. Mirelo SFX 2.0, which rebuilds the sound design of an AI clip without touching the picture, was saved more often than it was liked, and Krea 3 opened as an image model made for editing rather than making from scratch. What it means: the gap between a rough idea and a finished, moving, sound-designed piece keeps shrinking, so taste and a clear brief matter more than any single tool.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Monday, Oct 19, 2026
editions.summary: The design story that broke out today is Viggle's JST-2, a "physics-native world model" that builds scenes, characters and motion directly in 3D instead of generating flat video frames. Viggle says a scene takes about one second of model time and costs under a cent, that a single photo becomes a 3D character with motion built in and no rigging step, and that you can try it free today. The launch post passed 670K views with more than 800 saves, and it landed on the same day as the most-liked design post of the day: a WebGPU demo of jumping through portals between Gaussian-splat worlds in real time. It matters because 3D has been the slowest, most specialist part of a design pipeline. If photo-to-character and photo-to-scene really work in a browser, you can put real 3D in front of clients without a rigging artist or a game engine. Treat the hype carefully, though. Much of today's JST-2 chatter came as a wave of near-identical "free today" posts that read like a coordinated launch push, and Viggle itself says object physics is still rule-based until JST-3.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: Twelve weeks and $850–900 for a fishing game, films blocked in Three.js first, and models priced by the minute
editions.summary: A solo developer is twelve weeks into Nightshoal, a fishing-and-exploration game built almost entirely with Claude Opus 5.5. He has published what it cost: about $850–900 in AI and tooling so far. He also keeps a Decisions.md that logs which design calls were his and which were the AI's. That's the pattern in today's real-world uses: the people getting finished work out of AI plan first, give each tool one job, and publish their receipts, failures included.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: OpenAI's next image model slipped out. The open side answered with tools.
editions.summary: Three unreleased OpenAI image models, codenamed Aurora, surfaced in the API and then in Arena over the weekend, and testers can't agree whether they're a step forward. While that argument ran, the open-source side shipped: a blur-fixing MOSS-Image fine-tune, native MOSS support in ComfyUI, and a wave of free, local alternatives to Higgsfield for MiniMax H3 video. 78 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Sunday, Oct 18, 2026
editions.summary: This was the week the code-first design fight went three-way. For a month the hottest AI design work has been animation, 3D and UI written as code by Claude Opus 5.5, and the month's most-saved design post is simply a list of the open-source repos that make it work. Then Gemini 4 Argon arrived on Oct 13 and several of its most-shared launch demos were design work: an exploded-view product film built in Blender from a raw CAD file, a 3D-printing CAD studio in Canvas, and a camera you can play like a synth. Four days later DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 landed as an open model, and within a day creators were racing it against Opus and Argon on the same motion-graphics prompts for a fraction of the cost. On the image side the open models kept coming, and the ComfyUI builds of FLUX 3 Image Klein and MOSS-Image are each past 330,000 downloads. What it means: the skill that matters is giving a model good taste, references and a way to check its own work, because the models themselves are getting cheaper and easier to swap.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Sunday, Oct 18, 2026
editions.summary: The loudest design story of the weekend is DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an MIT-licensed open-weights update that creators spent two days pitting against Claude Opus 5.5 on code-built motion graphics, 3D scenes and frontends. The announcement is the most-engaged AI post in today's sweep by a wide margin, the model sits at the top of Hugging Face's trending list, and one of the big AI video platforms called it "the new SOTA for motion design" after running its own tests. It matters because the hottest design technique of the month, motion and 3D written as code instead of rendered by a video model, has so far meant paying for a frontier model. If a free, open model holds up, that whole way of working gets much cheaper and can run on your own hardware. The verdict isn't settled, though: side-by-side tests are mixed, and a few came out with blown-out colours.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: A car that didn't exist, a house no one opened in Blender, and 102 clips that all passed QA
editions.summary: Standard Chartered is an official F1 partner with no F1 team, so the 2026 car in its new film 'Move Ahead' never existed. Co-director Marcello Costa drew it by hand, had AI turn the sketch into 3D and extrapolate the angles, and placed every decal with the agency. He calls single-detail edits 'like 50-50' and says full AI isn't automatically cheaper. That's this edition's pattern: the work that holds up starts with a human draft, locks references, and checks the output, whether it's a bank ad, an archviz set or a dragon boss.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: An open model just walked into the motion-design studio
editions.summary: DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017 with MIT weights on Oct 17, and within hours creators were running it against Opus 5.5 on code-built motion graphics, 3D scenes and frontends. Around it: a 25-minute anime written entirely as code, MOSS-Image becoming Reddit's favourite open base model, and solo game builders settling on a repeatable method. 77 verified items from the last day.

editions.title: Hottest Right Now
editions.headline: AI Design Hottest Right Now · Saturday, Oct 17, 2026
editions.summary: The big story of the week and the month is the same one: the hottest AI design work is being made as code you can edit, not as pixels you regenerate. Figma's Config India launch put real website code on the canvas as Code Layers, the most-saved 3D posts have Claude write Python that builds every Blender model piece by piece, and a month of motion-design clips came from code-only animation with no video model at all. Meanwhile the image race got crowded and cheap fast: Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, Nano Banana 2.1, FLUX 3 Image Klein and Krea 3 all landed within ten days, and the open-weights ones are already running in ComfyUI. The practical takeaway is that taste files, scripts and design systems are becoming the thing a designer actually owns.

editions.title: Best of the Day
editions.headline: AI Design Best of the Day · Saturday, Oct 17, 2026
editions.summary: The idea people kept saving today is a change in how 3D gets made. Instead of sculpting, creators have Claude Opus 5.5 write Python that builds each model part by part inside Blender, then rerun the script when something needs to change. A how-to thread on exactly that became one of the day's most-saved design posts, a case study of a Steam game built this way is circulating widely, and a steady stream of first-timers posted their own "vibe-modeled" assets within hours. It matters because it turns 3D from a craft skill into something you can direct, version and fix by editing a number, which is a different job for designers, not just a faster one.

editions.title: AI Design in Use
editions.headline: How people actually used AI design tools this week: 94 real uses
editions.summary: A solo developer shipping a Steam fishing game didn't model anything by hand: one Claude Code session wrote and ran Blender scripts for every crab, gull and palm. A crab went from a four-sentence brief to animated on the beach in 53 minutes. That's this edition's pattern: the people getting real results use AI as a scriptable crew they direct, check and correct, not as a slot machine.

editions.title: AI Design Daily
editions.headline: Open image models had the week, and agents learned to drive Blender
editions.summary: FLUX 3 Klein, Krea 3 and MOSS-Image all landed within about 24 hours, Kling 4.0 went global, and the most-bookmarked creative technique of the week was Claude Opus 5.5 building 3D models through Blender MCP. 87 verified items from Oct 10–17.
